title: Touring the British Isles in 1948: Cardiff and the Royal Theater
summary: She toured to Wales, played Cardiff and the Royal Theater, and had a great reception.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe

blocks.x: But in '48, they -- when I went over there, I -- let me see. No, it was '53 when I really
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
toured the British Isles. I got to Wales. I played the -- what's the big theater there?
Yeah. I played in Cardiff. I played in Cardiff and -- Oh you talk about a tour! I left London and I got to Dublin, Ireland on St. Patrick's Day and I played --
That must have been an experience.

Oh boy! And I played the Royal Theater, which was a great experience. And then, I played Cardiff. No, I played Dundee and Aberdeen, and I left Dundee on a train for Cardiff, and the whole bit -- you know what I mean? And I was travelling, what I think, for days. That was a lot of travelling. But I had a ball in Cardiff -- we played the theater and I've visited some of the mills -- one of the textile mills there. I had a ball! I mean, I met so many
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

people, I don't even know who all I met. But I went to the mill and they gave me a piece of -- I said I wanted this wool. And they gave me a big piece of wool. I said, "I'm going to make a dress to wear at the evening show, the last show of the theater." So I went to the store and I bought some other material. I actually cut out and made a dress to wear to the last show. Cardiff, I mean, it was warm. In England -- oh. First of all, the first time I went was in July. It wasn't too bad. It was cold enough. But the next time I went in '54, it was cold. And I mean cold and damp --
Right. I told you I stayed with Adelaide and --
She'd been there for a long time by then.
